HOME SCIENCE MARCH — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Yeast Products.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Yeast Products.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Special Treatment in Laundry Work? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment 2.2 Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treat.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.

15. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.

17. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Convenience Foods? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Convenience Foods.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Convenience Foods.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Convenience Foods.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Convenience Foods.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

22. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
